title: Fleet silent-corruption probability
caption: With $\DeviceCount$ independent devices each carrying residual error probability $p$ per interval, at least one silent error somewhere in the fleet is a routine event, not a tail case. A per-device reliability number becomes a coordination cost.

symbols.name: per-device SDC probability
symbols.meaning: Residual silent-corruption probability for one device over the interval

symbols.name: device count
symbols.meaning: Number of independent devices in the fleet

symbols.name: fleet incidence
symbols.meaning: Probability at least one device experiences a silent error in the interval

title: Population stability index
caption: Each bin contributes a nonnegative term, so PSI decomposes per bin and shows which feature range moved. The fleet convention bands are monitoring conventions, calibrated per service, not universal statistical thresholds.

symbols.name: current proportion
symbols.meaning: Share of current traffic in bin i

symbols.name: reference proportion
symbols.meaning: Share of the baseline reference in bin i

symbols.name: bin count
symbols.meaning: Number of value-range bins cut on the reference sample

symbols.name: population stability index
symbols.meaning: Aggregate divergence score across the bins

title: Coverage and selective risk
caption: Raising the acceptance threshold $\tau$ reduces coverage; it lowers accepted-request risk only when the score orders requests by error risk well enough, measured on the deployment population. Rejected traffic does not disappear: it prices the fallback path.

symbols.name: acceptance threshold
symbols.meaning: Minimum acceptance score for answering directly

symbols.name: accepted set
symbols.meaning: Inputs whose acceptance score meets the threshold

symbols.name: loss
symbols.meaning: Loss of the prediction against the observed outcome

symbols.name: input
symbols.meaning: A serving request drawn from the deployment population

title: Conformal finite-sample coverage
caption: With $q$ at rank $\lceil(n{+}1)(1{-}\alpha)\rceil$ of $n$ calibration nonconformity scores, coverage is a finite-sample marginal guarantee under exchangeability. It is not conditional on subgroup: a rare slice can be poorly covered while the aggregate holds.

symbols.name: nonconformity score
symbols.meaning: How poorly candidate outcome y agrees with input X; larger means less conforming

symbols.name: score quantile
symbols.meaning: Calibration cutoff at the corrected rank

symbols.name: miscoverage rate
symbols.meaning: Target fraction of requests allowed outside the prediction set

symbols.name: calibration size
symbols.meaning: Number of held-out calibration examples

symbols.name: prediction set
symbols.meaning: Set of candidate labels retained for input X

title: Fast gradient sign method
caption: One backward pass, one step to a corner of the $\ell_\infty$ budget cube. At $\epsilon=0.007$ it flips GoogLeNet from panda at 57.7 percent confidence to gibbon at 99.3 percent. A single step need not maximize the nonlinear loss or cause misclassification.

symbols.name: adversarial example
symbols.meaning: Perturbed input after the single step

symbols.name: perturbation budget
symbols.meaning: Maximum per-coordinate change under the l-infinity norm

symbols.name: input gradient
symbols.meaning: Local sensitivity of the loss to each input coordinate

symbols.name: model parameters
symbols.meaning: Trained weights, fixed during the attack

title: Gaussian KL divergence
caption: Closed form for fitted Gaussian baseline and current densities. Exact for the density models; its fidelity to the transaction populations depends on the fit. Moderate values warrant investigation, not automatic retraining.

symbols.name: baseline fit
symbols.meaning: Mean and standard deviation fitted to the reference window

symbols.name: current fit
symbols.meaning: Mean and standard deviation fitted to the current window

symbols.name: KL divergence
symbols.meaning: Divergence of the current density from the baseline

title: Huber loss
caption: Quadratic inside the threshold, linear beyond it, so a surviving poisoned outlier grows linearly where squared error keeps squaring. At 100 times the normal residual, squared loss pays 10,000 times while Huber pays about 100.

symbols.name: residual
symbols.meaning: Prediction error of one training example

symbols.name: threshold
symbols.meaning: Residual scale where the loss transitions from quadratic to linear

symbols.name: Huber loss
symbols.meaning: Robust loss bounding the influence of extreme residuals

title: Influence of a training point
caption: Approximates how upweighting training point $z$ moves the test loss at $z_t$ without retraining, using inverse-Hessian-vector products. Approximate in deep nonconvex networks; validate against the architecture before treating it as attribution.

symbols.name: training point
symbols.meaning: Candidate training example whose weight is perturbed

symbols.name: test point
symbols.meaning: Example whose loss change is approximated

symbols.name: Hessian
symbols.meaning: Curvature matrix of the average training loss at the fitted parameters

symbols.name: loss gradient
symbols.meaning: Gradient of the point loss with respect to the parameters
